the apparent elastic modulus E of compliant polymer thin film substrata decreases with decreasing film thickness, and that the apparent modulus E of these films is independent of the angle of indentation.

the apparent stiffness of polymeric films of thicknesses less than 100 nm can be accurately measured using contact models, if the indentation angle of the indenter is kept constant and the indentation depth is kept less than 5 % of the film thickness.
the apparent elastic modulus of nanoscale films of polymeric materials is strongly dependent on the film thickness and indentation angle.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the contact mechanics of compliant materials is highly sensitive to thickness and the angle of indentation, and that this must be taken into account when extracting mechanical properties of nanoscale films.
